newsitem.title: FRANCE: Finance panel head concerned about BoF nominations.
newsitem.headline: Finance panel head concerned about BoF nominations.

text.p: Pierre Mehaignerie, chairman of the French National Assembly's finance commission, said on Friday he was concerned by the government's decision not to renew Jean Boissonnat's mandate on the Bank of France monetary policy council.

"This choice saddens and worries me," Mehaignerie said in a statement. "There is a contradiction between, on the one hand, the president's declarations on building Europe and the need to adapt French society, and, on the other hand, the removal of a man of conviction who was one of the strongest advocates of such a project."
The government on Friday nominated Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard to the monetary policy council, replacing two outgng Boissonnat -- viewed as being from the strong franc camp.
The two new candidates are viewed by the financial markets as being more favourable to interest rate cuts.

But Prime Minister Alain Juppe said the nominations did not signal a change in direction. President Jacques Chirac called on the Bank of France "to conduct monetary policy in stability and continuity," Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said.
Lamassoure also said interest rate levels were not an obstacle to growth.
